newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Norilsk Nickel hits Russian shares.
newsitem.headline: Norilsk Nickel hits Russian shares.

text.p: Leading Russian shares closed mixed in sluggish late afternoon trading, dealers said, as Norilsk Nickel metals producer slid on financial troubles and Western investors stayed home.
But they said short-covering on Tuesday could pull levels up slightly.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index closed slightly up, at 356.52 after 356.27 on Friday. But total market turnover was a limp $20 million.
"I think the market will be slightly stronger tomorrow and everything will go up a little bit," said senior United City Bank trader Samit Yakovlev.
"Orders collapsed a bit today simply because there were no clients, but they should appear tomorrow."

Norilsk Nickel fell over 12 percent to close at $6.40 after $7.33 at Friday's close, but off an early low of $6.35 earlier in the morning, on a 3.29 trillion rouble consolidated 1996 loss released on Friday after market close.
Norilsk also said plans to issue American Depositary Receipts soon to allow foreign trade could be affected by the 1996 financial results.
Traders said aggressive selling of Norilsk, had fallen off towards the end of the day, but said it could fall further.

"Ten percent for these shares is not the limit -- clients will sell," said UCB's Yakovlev. "In any case the information is sad. I cannot say that today's fall is a good opportunity to buy, unless we're talking about long-term investors."
Natural gas producer Gazprom, whose bankers ABN-Amro and Goldman Sachs said on Monday it would raise $2-3 billion on Western capital markets within six months, rose to $0.6625 from $0.6550 on Friday.
But Yakovlev downplayed the significance of the announcement.
"In my opinion, nothing fundamental is happening in Gazprom," said Yakovlev. "The Eurobond news has given confidence to regular, big buyers."
